problem: The nonblocking assignment operator <= has been lost, so the text reads 'Use nonblocking  in sequential always blocks', 'Mixing = and  in one clocked always block. Use  for every state register update', and 'Why is nonblocking  used in a clocked always block?'. The student sees a blank where the most important operator of the section should be, and the contrast with blocking = is destroyed.
fix: Restore the operator in all three places: 'Use nonblocking <= in sequential always blocks', 'Mixing = and <= in one clocked always block. Use <= for every state register update', 'Why is nonblocking <= used in a clocked always block?'. Escape the less-than character in the source (as <) so it is not swallowed when the page is rendered.

problem: The typical statement shown is 'always @(*) if (sel) y = b;' with no else. Copied as written, this holds y when sel=0 and infers a latch, which contradicts the latch warning two paragraphs above.
fix: Show a complete statement, e.g. 'always @(*) y = sel ? b : a;' or 'always @(*) if (sel) y = b; else y = a;'.

problem: 'Gate level uses four instances of a 1-bit mux or gates' is loose: Verilog has no 1-bit mux primitive, so a mux can only be an instance of a user module (structural) or be built from gate primitives.
fix: Say: 'Gate level uses four instances of a 1-bit mux module, or gate primitives wired as a mux.'
